changes.before: Change twice(3) to twice(4) but keep static_assert(size == 6). What happens?
changes.after: Calculate a constant and check it before the program runs.

before: A constexpr function can participate in constant evaluation when its inputs and operations permit it. Calling that function does not by itself force every call to happen at compile time.
constexpr int size = twice(3) requires a constant expression. By contrast, an ordinary int can hold a runtime result even when the called function is declared constexpr.
static_assert requires a constant condition. A false condition rejects the program during compilation, before main runs. This is different from a runtime assert that may be disabled in some builds.
Expected output or behavior: 6. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Keep the function constexpr but call it with a runtime input; explain which values still qualify for static_assert. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: Compile time is when source code is turned into a program. A constexpr function can be evaluated then when its inputs and operations allow it. Other calls to the same function may still run later.
constexpr int size requires its starting value to be a constant expression, one the compiler can evaluate. Here twice(3) meets that requirement.
static_assert checks a constant condition during compilation. If the condition is false, the compiler rejects the program and reports the supplied message.
The program prints 6. The compiler calculates size as six, and the size == 6 assertion passes before main runs.

A runtime check happens while a program is running. static_assert happens earlier and requires a constant condition. The separate assert facility is a runtime check that some build settings can disable.

before.question: Change twice(3) to twice(4) but keep static_assert(size == 6). What happens?
choices: The program prints 8 and then warns.
The compiler changes size back to 6.
Compilation fails; there is no successful program run.
before.explanation: size becomes the constant 8. The required compile-time assertion 8 == 6 is false.

after.question: Change twice(3) to twice(4), but keep static_assert(size == 6). What happens?
choices: The program prints 8 and then gives a warning.
The compiler changes size back to 6.
Compilation fails, so this changed program cannot run successfully.
after.explanation: size becomes the constant eight. The assertion that it equals six is false, so the compiler rejects the program.
